readings.title: Eliphaz Continues
readings.subtitle: The Discipline of Eloah
readings.text: [Job 5:1] “Call out now, is there anyone to answer you? And to which of the set-apart ones do you turn? [2] “For wrath kills a fool, and envy slays a simple one. [3] “I have seen the fool taking root, but suddenly I cursed his home. [4] “His sons are far from safety, and they are crushed in the gate, with no deliverer. [5] “Because the hungry eat his harvest, taking it even from the thorns, and a snare snaps up their wealth. [6] “For evil does not come from the dust, nor does trouble spring from the ground; [7] “For man is born for trouble, as sparks fly upward. [8] “But I, I would seek <dn>Ěl</dn>, and to <dn>Elohim</dn> I would commit my cause, [9] “Who does great things, and unsearchable, marvellous deeds without number; [10] “Who gives rain on the face of the earth, and sends water on the face of the fields; [11] “To set up the lowly on high, and those who mourn shall be lifted to safety. [12] “<dn>He</dn> frustrates the schemes of the crafty, so that their hands do not do what they planned. [13] “<dn>He</dn> catches the wise in their own craftiness, and the counsel of the twisted is hastened. [14] “By day they meet with darkness, and grope at noon as in the night. [15] “But <dn>He</dn> saves the needy from the sword, from their mouth, and from the hand of the mighty. [16] “So the poor have hope, and unrighteousness shall shut her mouth. [17] “Look, blessed is the man whom <dn>Eloah</dn> reproves, so do not despise the discipline of the <dn>Almighty</dn>. [18] “For <dn>He</dn> bruises, but <dn>He</dn> binds up; <dn>He</dn> smites, but <dn>His</dn> hands heal. [19] “In six distresses <dn>He</dn> delivers you, and in seven no evil touches you. [20] “In scarcity of food <dn>He</dn> shall redeem you from death, and in battle from the power of the sword. [21] “You shall be hidden from the scourge of the tongue, and not be afraid of destruction when it comes. [22] “You shall laugh at destruction and starvation, and not be afraid of the beasts of the earth. [23] “For your covenant is with the stones of the field, and the beasts of the field are at peace with you. [24] “And you shall know that your tent is in peace, and you shall visit your fold and miss nothing. [25] “And you shall know that your seed is many, and your offspring like the grass of the earth. [26] “You shall come to the grave in a ripe age, like a stack of grain coming up in its season. [27] “Look, this we have searched out, it is true. Hear it, and know it for yourself.”

readings.title: Job's Reply to Eliphaz
readings.subtitle: My Grief is Heavier than Sand
readings.text: [Job 6:1] Then Iyoḇ answered and said, [2] “Oh, that my grief were weighed, and my calamity laid in the scales together! [3] “For now it would be heavier than the sand of the sea – therefore my words have been rash. [4] “For the arrows of the <dn>Almighty</dn> are within me, my spirit drinks in their poison, the terrors of <dn>Eloah</dn> set themselves in array against me. [5] “Does the wild donkey bray when it has grass? Or does the ox low over its fodder? [6] “Is tasteless food eaten without salt? Or is there any taste in the white of an egg? [7] “My soul refused to touch them, they are as my loathsome food. [8] “Oh, that I might have my request, that <dn>Eloah</dn> would grant my expectation! [9] “That it would please <dn>Eloah</dn> to crush me, that <dn>He</dn> would loose <dn>His</dn> hand and cut me off! [10] “Then I would still have comfort, and I would rejoice in pain – though <dn>He</dn> does not spare – for I have not hidden the words of the Set-apart One. [11] “What is my strength, that I should wait? And what is my end, that I should prolong my life? [12] “Is my strength the strength of stones? Or is my flesh bronze? [13] “Is my help not within me? And is substance driven from me? [14] “To him who is melting, kindness is due from his friend, lest he forsake the fear of the <dn>Almighty</dn>. [15] “My brothers have acted deceitfully like a wadi, like the streams of wadis that pass away, [16] “Which are black because of ice, and into which the snow vanishes. [17] “When it becomes hot, they are cut off; in the heat they vanish from their place. [18] “The paths of their way turn aside, they go into the wasteland and perish. [19] “The caravans of Tĕma looked, the travellers of Sheḇa waited for them. [20] “They were ashamed because they had trusted, they came there and were confused. [21] “For now you are like it, you see my casting down and are afraid. [22] “Did I say, ‘Give to me’? Or, ‘Offer a bribe for me from your wealth’? [23] “Or, ‘Deliver me from the enemy’s hand’? Or, ‘Redeem me from the hand of oppressors’? [24] “Teach me, and I keep silent; and cause me to understand wherein I have erred. [25] “How powerful are right words! But what does your reproof reprove? [26] “Do you reckon to reprove words, and the speeches of a desperate one, which are as wind? [27] “You would even cast lots for an orphan, and feast on your friend. [28] “And now, please look at me, and see if I lie to your face. [29] “Turn back, please, let there be no unrighteousness; and turn back, my righteousness is still in it. [30] “Is there unrighteousness on my tongue? Does my palate not discern calamity? [Job 7:1] “Is there not a time of hard service for man on earth? Are his days also like the days of a hired man? [2] “Like a servant he pants for a shadow, and like a hired man he waits for his wages. [3] “So I have been made to possess months of emptiness, and nights of trouble have been appointed to me. [4] “When I lie down, I say, ‘When do I arise, and the night be ended?’ For I have had my fill of tossings till dawn. [5] “My flesh is clothed with worms and dust; my skin is cracked and breaks out afresh.

readings.title: A Plea for Relief
readings.subtitle: Why Have You Set Me as a Target?
readings.text: [Job 7:6] “My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle, and are spent without hope. [7] “Remember that my life is a breath; my eye is not to see good again. [8] “The eye of him who sees me sees me no more; while your eyes are upon me, I am no more. [9] “As a cloud disappears and vanishes away, so he who goes down to the grave does not come up. [10] “He returns no more to his house, nor does his place know him anymore. [11] “I also, I do not hold my mouth; I speak in the distress of my spirit, I complain in the bitterness of my soul. [12] “Am I a sea, or a sea-monster, that <dn>You</dn> set a guard over me? [13] “When I say, ‘My bed comforts me, my couch eases my complaint,’ [14] “Then <dn>You</dn> scare me with dreams and terrify me with visions, [15] “So that my being chooses strangling, death rather than my bones. [16] “I have rejected it; I would not live forever. Let me alone, for my days are but a breath. [17] “What is man that <dn>You</dn> magnify him? And that <dn>You</dn> set <dn>Your</dn> heart upon him? [18] “And that <dn>You</dn> visit him every morning, try him every moment? [19] “How long would <dn>You</dn> not look away from me, nor let me alone till I swallow my spittle? [20] “Have I sinned? What have I done to <dn>You</dn>, O Watcher of men? Why have <dn>You</dn> set me as a target for <dn>You</dn>, so that I am a burden to myself? [21] “And why do <dn>You</dn> not pardon my transgression and take away my crookedness? For now I lie down in the dust, and <dn>You</dn> shall seek me, but I am no more.”

readings.title: Bildad Speaks
readings.subtitle: Does El Pervert Justice?
readings.text: [Job 8:1] Then Bildad the Shuḥite answered and said, [2] “How long would you speak these words? And the words of your mouth be a great wind? [3] “Does <dn>Ěl</dn> pervert right-ruling? Or does the <dn>Almighty</dn> pervert justice? [4] “If your sons have sinned against <dn>Him</dn>, then <dn>He</dn> has delivered them into the hand of their transgression. [5] “If you would earnestly seek <dn>Ěl</dn>, and make your supplication to the <dn>Almighty</dn>, [6] “If you were pure and straight, surely now <dn>He</dn> would awake for you, and prosper your righteous dwelling place. [7] “And though your beginning was small, yet your latter end would increase greatly. [8] “For please ask the former generation, and prepare yourself for the search of their fathers. [9] “For we are but of yesterday, and know not, because our days on earth are a shadow. [10] “Do they not teach you and speak to you, and bring forth words from their heart? [11] “Does papyrus grow up without a marsh? Does reed grow without water? [12] “While it is yet green and not cut down, it withers before any plant. [13] “So are the paths of all who forget <dn>Ěl</dn>. And the hope of the godless one perishes, [14] “Whose trust is cut off, and whose trust is a spider’s web. [15] “He leans on his house, but it does not stand; he holds it fast, but it does not endure. [16] “He is green before the sun, and his branches spread out in his garden. [17] “His roots are wrapped around a heap of stones; he looks for a house of stones. [18] “If he is destroyed from his place, then it denies him, saying, ‘I have not seen you.’ [19] “See, this is the joy of <dn>His</dn> way, and out of the dust others spring up. [20] “See, <dn>Ěl</dn> does not reject the perfect, nor does <dn>He</dn> strengthen the hand of evil-doers. [21] “<dn>He</dn> would yet fill your mouth with laughter, and your lips with shouting. [22] “Those who hate you are clothed with shame, and the tent of the wrong is no more.”
